prompt: Open sea seen from high above, filling the whole image edge to edge with water. In the upper right quarter only, a small group of tiny round buoys on two thin ropes: the two ropes come from slightly different directions and meet at one last buoy, joining there like two paths merging into one. That last buoy carries a little plain cobalt blue #3D6FD9 pennant flag on a thin mast, the pennant marked with a single bold off-white tick, one simple V-shaped stroke. The buoys are small, no bigger than a fingertip in the image. Buoys and ropes drawn in crisp off-white and ink grey line art with fine engraved shading, small ripples drawn as lines around each buoy. The left half and the whole bottom of the image are calm open water with only gentle wave lines. Richly detailed engraved nautical chart style, like a fine antique sea chart printed in two inks: the sea built from many layers of fine wave lines and hatching, line density increasing towards the deep water to give depth, tonal bands from deep cerulean at the bottom to lighter cerulean at the top, bathymetric contour lines with small depth soundings drawn as tiny dots, subtle foam strokes and a few glints of light on the crests. Every wave is drawn as visible engraved line work, like a steel engraving, never painted, never smooth. Crisp sharp lines of several weights, intricate but calm, premium print quality, high detail, elegant. No realistic objects, no photographic rendering, no glow, no text, no letters, no numbers, no watermark, full-bleed. Palette strictly limited to medium cerulean ocean blue #0072a8 and its tints and shades, off-white #fbfcfd, ink grey #13212b and a touch of cobalt blue #3D6FD9 on the pennant only.
